newsitem.title: LATVIA: METROMEDIA EYES LATVIAN COMMS MARKET.
newsitem.headline: METROMEDIA EYES LATVIAN COMMS MARKET.

text.p: Metromedia International Telecommunications (MITI), an American firm affiliated with Latvian-American joint-venture Baltcom GSM, said on Tuesday that it was eyeing additional opportunities in Latvia.
"We are looking for other communications opportunities where ever they present themselves," Stuart Subotnik, MITI's managing director, said at a news conference.
The company has already invested some $40 million in Latvia's cable, paging and celluar phone markets and Subotnic said it planned to invest a further $25 to $30 million in these areas.
"We have had reasonable success in both cable and paging in Latvia, and we think that GSM's celluar phone network will also be a success," Subtonic said.
He said that the company saw lucrative markets in other communications sectors.
"We are looking for possibilities in wireless services, international toll calling and trunk mobile radio services or dispatches," he said.
He added that the company required licenses before it could set up operations in these areas.
"We would also be interested in providing additional phone services," he said.
The company currently has operations in several Eastern European countries and former Soviet republics.
